summary: This bill lowers the minimum age from 21 to 18 for buying a handgun from a federally licensed dealer by amending 18 U.S.C. 922(b)(1) to eliminate the under-21 restriction for handguns and making a conforming change to 922(c)(1).

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgets. It solely amends firearm purchase age requirements under existing law.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation does not address healthcare policy, insurance, providers, or public health programs.

The bill directly amends 18 U.S.C. § 922(b)(1) and § 922(c)(1) to lower the minimum age for purchasing handguns from federal firearms licensees from 21 to 18. This reduces an existing federal restriction on firearm acquisition and is framed explicitly as advancing Second Amendment rights, placing it strongly on the gun-rights side of the spectrum.
